title: Thingstudio processor definition
description: A ~/.thingstudio/processors/<id>.json file, or a built-in under editor/src/definitions/processors/. The file name without .json is the id (lowercase letters, digits, - and _). Authoritative prose: interfaces/board-descriptor/SPEC.md; user walkthrough: docs/user-guide/boards.md.

name.description: Name shown in the Board menu.

match.description: Substrings matched against the MCU part of HELLO's chipType (after ' with '), case-, space- and dash-insensitive.

nativeArchConfirmed.description: false marks nativeArch as a guess (shown as unverified). Default true.

capabilities.description: Hardware features the chip has, e.g. "wifi", "ble", "espnow", "pio". A node's requires.capabilities is checked against these at compile time.

gpio.description: Every pin the processor has (GPIO numbers, or named pins). Required, at least one pin.

inputOnly.description: Pins that cannot drive an output. Must be in gpio.

noPull.description: Pins with no internal pull resistors. Must be in gpio.

adc2.description: Pins on the chip's second ADC (ESP32 family), unusable while WiFi is up. Must be in gpio. Empty/absent when there is none.

reserved.description: Pins that must not be used, with a reason each. Keys must be in gpio.

avoid.description: Pins that warn, with a reason each. Keys must be in gpio.

spi.description: SPI buses and speed limits. Omit for a processor with no SPI.

maxHz.description: Top SPI clock on the bus's own pins.

otherPinsMaxHz.description: Top SPI clock on other pins (ESP32 GPIO matrix).

buses.description: Bus id (a number as a string, e.g. "1") -> bus. Use {} for a usable bus with any pins.

fastPins.description: Pins that reach the bus without the GPIO matrix (ESP32 family). Not a restriction.

pins.description: When present, the ONLY pins this bus can use per role (RP2 family).

i2c.description: I2C buses. Omit for a processor with no I2C.

pins.description: When present, the ONLY pins this bus can use per role (RP2 family).

notes.description: Anything worth knowing, shown on the Pins page.

flash.description: How a board on this chip is written from blank: the tool, esptool's chip id, and where an image starts. Omit when the editor cannot flash it (no dfu yet).

pinId.description: A named pin on a processor whose pins aren't numbered, e.g. the pyboard's "X1" or "A13".

pinList.description: Pins as numbers (0-255), range strings like "4-7", or named pins like "X1".

pinReasons.description: Pin or range (as a key, e.g. "6-11", or a name) -> a non-empty reason.

flash.description: How a board on this chip is written from blank. esptool writes the ESP32 family over a serial port; uf2 copies to a mounted drive (RP2040/RP2350, nRF52).

chip.description: esptool's chip id (esp32, esp32s2, esp32s3, esp32c3, ...). Omit to let esptool identify the chip. Not allowed for uf2.

address.description: Where the image goes, in bytes: 4096 (0x1000) for ESP32 and ESP32-S2, 0 for the rest. Not allowed for uf2.
